clue.text: Proving what showers are doing?

definitions.meaning: proving a point is showing it to be true
read 'showers' as people who show things, not rain or bathroom fittings: they are putting things on display

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about rain or bathroom fittings, set against a word about proof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showers' wants to be rain or a place to wash; here it means people who show something.
explanation.definitionFit: To prove a theory is to establish it by evidence, and putting things on view for others is the job of anyone who shows.

clue.text: Wrongly claimed invention, which put Bob out.

indicators.note: something done wrongly is done out of order, so the letters of claimed are reworked

parts.note: coinage can mean the invention of a new word or phrase

explanation.surface: A complaint that some invention was falsely claimed, which annoyed a man named Bob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a person who was upset; it is old British slang for a shilling, a coin abolished when Britain went decimal in 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1971 switch to pounds and pence retired the shilling, nicknamed a bob, so the new currency system drove it out.

clue.text: He has little reason for extra clothes, say

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is to be heard spoken, not spelt

parts.note: putting extra clothes on means having more on

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a man is unreasonable for wanting more layers of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More on' (more clothes on) spoken quickly sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool or idiot is a person with very little power of reasoning.

clue.text: Such a view is urged before death

definitions.text: Such a view is urged before death

parts.words: Such a view is urged before death
parts.note: refers to the proverb 'See Naples and die': a sight of that Italian city is supposedly the last thing worth having before you die

explanation.surface: Someone is told to take in a particular view before they die.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'See Naples and die' says the city is so beautiful that nothing more remains to be seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Something belonging to Naples is described by the Italian city's adjective, and the proverb recommends that view before dying.

clue.text: Coming down fast, to join up with most of 12

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to meet is to join or come together

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the referenced answer is dropped

parts.note: the answer to 12 across, the dean INGE

explanation.surface: Something descending quickly is told to link up with most of another clue's answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns MEET to TEEM; 'most of' drops the last letter of INGE (12 across) to leave ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain that teems is pouring heavily, falling in torrents.

clue.text: Mixture of seaweed seen in a short distance

indicators.note: seen in says the seaweed is placed inside the short distance

parts.note: MM, millimetres, a very short distance
alga is a seaweed or similar simple plant

explanation.surface: A mixture of seaweed is spotted just a little way off.
explanation.definitionFit: An amalgam is a blend, originally an alloy of mercury with another metal.

clue.text: Hardly Long Island

definitions.meaning: a tiny length, scarcely long at all
in Scotland and Ireland an ... is a small island

explanation.definitionFit: The measure is only 2.5 centimetres, barely long, and in Scottish place names (Inchcolm) the same word means a small island.

clue.text: Fool arranged 13 for March

parts.note: goose is an old word for a silly person

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of the referenced answer are put into a new order

parts.note: the answer to 13 across, PEST

explanation.surface: A silly person rearranged something for the month of March.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like the month; it is the verb. 'arranged' turns PEST (13 across) into STEP.
explanation.definitionFit: The goose-step is a stiff-legged way of marching associated with parading soldiers.

clue.text: Ignored, like German bombers in November 1940

definitions.meaning: being shunned or given the silent treatment
the Luftwaffe raid on Coventry in November 1940 sent its bombers to that English city

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means being shunned by everyone, and literally the Luftwaffe dispatched its planes on the devastating 14 November 1940 raid on that Midlands city.

clue.text: Backing some roan eg at races in Spain

indicators.note: Backing says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone is betting on a roan horse, for instance, at race meetings in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like betting on a horse; it says to read the letters right to left. The definition is just 'in Spain', a place there.
explanation.definitionFit: Cartagena is a port city on the south-east coast of Spain.

clue.text: Philosopher Peter's endless role in Church

indicators.note: in says the trimmed word goes inside the abbreviation for the church

parts.note: CE, the Church of England

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: the name Peter means rock, the role Christ gave him: 'on this rock I will build my church'

explanation.surface: A thinker named Peter has a never-ending part to play in the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peter' looks like the philosopher's first name; it stands for ROCK, his role as the church's foundation, and 'role' is a link. 'endless' cuts ROCK to ROC.
explanation.definitionFit: Benedetto Croce was an Italian philosopher and historian of the early twentieth century.

clue.text: Worker to repair tropical tree

parts.note: a man is a worker or employee, as in management and men
to repair to a place is to go there

explanation.surface: An employee is sent to fix a tree in the tropics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repair' looks like fixing; it means going somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The mango is an evergreen fruit tree grown across hot countries.

clue.text: In general dean gets primacy there

indicators.note: the dean's name comes first, at the very start of the words 'In general'

explanation.surface: Generally speaking, a church dean takes precedence in that place.
explanation.walkthrough: W. R. Inge was the famous 'gloomy dean' of St Paul's Cathedral; his name opens the words 'In general'.
explanation.definitionFit: William Ralph Inge was a celebrated Dean of St Paul's in London.

clue.text: Plague is first in Portugal, then is in France

indicators.note: first in means take only the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: est is French for is

explanation.surface: A plague breaks out first in Portugal and then in France.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a disease spreading across Europe; 'is in France' asks for the French word for is.
explanation.definitionFit: Pest is an old word for a deadly epidemic, and as a verb plague means to pester.

clue.text: Change for motorist?

parts.note: change here is changing gear, not coins: a driver shifts up from the lowest ratio

explanation.surface: A driver needs some small coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' suggests coins for a parking meter; it is a shift of the gear lever.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving the gear lever from first up to the next ratio is a change any driver makes.

clue.text: Drinking overtaking the hindmost of course

definitions.meaning: a cat drinks milk by scooping it with its tongue
a runner who catches a back marker on a circuit has gone a full circuit ahead

explanation.definitionFit: A cat drinks milk with its tongue, and a racer passing the slowest rival on a circuit puts them a full circuit behind.

clue.text: They appear with a flower hire-purchase set-up

indicators.note: set-up means an arrangement, so the letters are arranged anew

parts.note: the anemone is a flower
HP, the abbreviation for hire purchase, buying goods on instalments

explanation.surface: Someone rents a flower arrangement on instalment terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set-up' reorders ANEMONE plus HP. Hire purchase is the British name for buying on instalments.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomena are things that appear or are observed; the Greek root means appearing.

clue.text: Great performer, as seen intermittently in training in Paris

annotationWithheld.why: Great performer, as seen intermittently in training in Paris (7): MAESTRO is METRO (train in Paris) with the A and S of 'as' inserted at two separate points; one indicator ('seen intermittently in') splits one word into two inserted letters, which the grammar cannot express without indicator-less first/last picks and a nested container.
annotationWithheld.clue: Great performer, as seen intermittently in training in Paris

clue.text: Work of poet's to open class

parts.note: ope is a poetic, archaic form of the verb open
rate means class or grade, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: A poet's work is meant to open a class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' looks like a noun for the poem; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine works or functions when it runs, and to run it is to make it function.

clue.text: A little woolly as essayist, you said first

indicators.note: first places the spoken piece before the essayist
said signals that the word is to be heard spoken

parts.note: you, spoken, sounds like the female sheep
Charles Lamb wrote the Essays of Elia

explanation.surface: Someone is told they are rather woolly as a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woolly' looks like vague thinking; it is a young sheep. 'said' turns 'you' into its soundalike EWE, and 'first' puts it ahead of LAMB.
explanation.definitionFit: A female baby sheep is a small fleecy creature.

clue.text: Centre of horoscopist's arrangement, perhaps

indicators.note: an arrangement puts those core letters in a new order
centre of means drop the outer letters and keep the core of the word

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: An astrologer's chart might have one sign at its heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre of' keeps ROSCOPI, the middle seven letters of HOROSCOPIST, and 'arrangement' reorders them. The whole clue is also the definition: a sign of the zodiac at the heart of an astrologer's chart.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorpio is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac on which astrologers build their charts.

clue.text: Where some Italians live in New Orleans

indicators.note: new means the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A remark about Italian immigrants settling in New Orleans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Orleans' looks like the US city; 'New' is the signal to rearrange ORLEANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Salerno is a port city in southern Italy, home to many Italians.

clue.text: Contrary responses to request in quiet spot

parts.note: a refusal to a request is no
an agreement to a request is OK

explanation.surface: Someone asking a favour gets opposing answers in a peaceful corner.
explanation.walkthrough: The two opposite replies, refusal and consent, are set side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a secluded corner or recess.

clue.text: Sound of bells heard from this tower

indicators.note: heard says the word for the bells is to be taken as spoken

parts.note: a peal is the ringing of a set of bells

explanation.surface: Church bells ring out from a tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tower' suggests a bell tower; it is a small fortified tower of the Scottish Borders.
explanation.definitionFit: Peel towers were small fortified keeps built along the England-Scotland border.

clue.text: Put out in Arabian ship for a spell to sea ? Not quite

parts.note: a dow, or dhow, is an Arab sailing vessel

indicators.note: not quite means the last letter of the word is left off

parts.note: sea is taken as written before it is trimmed

explanation.surface: A sailor sets out to sea for a while in an Arab boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' looks like setting sail; it means extinguish. 'Not quite' trims SEA to SE; 'in' and 'for a spell to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To dowse, or douse, a flame or lamp is to extinguish it.

clue.text: To produce young women's leader needs support

indicators.note: leader means the opening letter of the word it goes with

parts.note: help is support or aid

explanation.surface: A woman producing a child needs the backing of her women's leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'young' looks like children; the definition is the verb, as of a dog giving birth.
explanation.definitionFit: To whelp is to give birth to puppies or cubs.

clue.text: Should typist encounter this, include everything written first

definitions.text: Should typist encounter this, include everything written first

parts.words: Should typist encounter this, include everything written first
parts.note: a proofreader's mark telling the typist to restore and keep the original wording that had been struck out

explanation.surface: An instruction telling a typist to keep all the original text.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin mark means 'let it stand': a crossed-out word is kept as first written.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin printer's mark means let it stand, cancelling a deletion in a manuscript or proof.

clue.text: Browning's source of good news

parts.note: Robert Browning's poem 'How They Brought the Good News from' a Belgian city 'to Aix'

explanation.surface: A poet's place for hearing happy tidings.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Browning's poem has horsemen galloping with good news from a Flemish city to Aix.
explanation.definitionFit: In Browning's ride poem the riders set out with their tidings from this Belgian city.

clue.text: Mere change in a factor achieves harmony

indicators.note: in says the reworked letters go inside the agent

parts.note: a factor is an agent who does business for another

indicators.note: change means the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A small change to a mathematical factor brings everything into balance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'factor' suggests a number in maths; here it is an old word for a business agent, someone who trades on another's behalf.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreement is concord between people, a state of being in harmony.

clue.text: Pay big author nothing, oddly, for life-work

indicators.note: oddly means arranged in a strange order, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A publisher pays a big-name author nothing, strangely, for a lifetime's achievement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'life-work' looks like a career's labour; it is a book that writes up the author's own life.
explanation.definitionFit: An autobiography is a written account of the writer's own life.
